topics.working_title: FCC Approves SpaceX's Plan to Put Up to 1 Million AI Data Center Satellites in Orbit
topics.why_now: The Verge, TechCrunch and Cointelegraph all covered the FCC's approval within hours of each other; it's the first such approval granted to any company (Google and Blue Origin are also pursuing orbital AI data centers), and Memeburn has no coverage yet.
topics.angle: Explain what 'Starmind' actually is (AI-chip-equipped satellites processing data in orbit for use on Earth), why companies want data centers in space (power/cooling), and what the FCC dismissed from opponents' concerns — a clear 'what it is and why now' explainer rather than a repeat of the press release.
headline_options: FCC Approves SpaceX's Plan to Put 1 Million AI Data Centers in Space
SpaceX's Starmind Satellites Just Got FCC Approval — Here's What That Means

sources.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX's plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space

topics.notes_for_writer: Note that Google and Blue Origin are pursuing similar orbital data-center concepts — worth a one-line comparison. Flag that the FCC dismissed some opponents' concerns (scientific research impact) only because they fell outside its regulatory authority, not because they were resolved.
